X.note: Clean CG render with an honest 'not a photograph' caption, a readable lower third and a year badge. The huge empty sky and bare sand fill most of the frame. Soldiers are peg-doll figures with no scale. Cannon and shot piles are sparse props. Facades are blank white boxes with a few dark holes. Nothing says Grand Parade or Main Street. The year badge is clear and the caption is legible, though the caption bar hides the lower-left corner.

Y.note: The aerial game-engine view has a better depth of field and a believable bay and hillside. The low-poly town has terracotta roofs. The tower is a lone, generic crenellated block with no real Gibraltar identity, and the 'Tower of Homage 23 m' label is dubious. The callout covers the town centre and the pointer line is hard to follow. The source line 'Ministry for Heritage' is a modern body, so it is not a credible 1884 source. The '≈18,659' population figure is falsely precise. The large flat green and brown terrain is empty. There are no people, ships, or harbour or industrial life of 1884.

why: Y has more varied composition, depth and built-up scene content, while X is mostly empty sky and sand with peg-doll figures, though X's text is more honest and readable.
top_fix_for_weaker: Frame X: crop or lower the camera to cut the empty sky, then fill the Parade with scaled, detailed soldiers, carts and civilians. Add real facade detail (balconies, shutters, arcades, roof lines) and a title that names Grand Parade/Main Street, and keep the 'not a photograph' caption.
